h: Seals on the Doorstep, Circus Round the Corner
p: One of the nicest things about an aquarium in Great Yarmouth is that the real thing isn't far away. The east Norfolk coast is famous for its seals, and grey seals haul out on the sandbanks off Scroby Sands, out near the wind farm you can see from the beach. Up the coast at Horsey, the winter pupping season brings crowds of visitors to see the fluffy white pups from the viewing areas, usually between November and January. Seeing the aquarium's displays first gives kids a head start on knowing what they're looking at.

Inside, it's worth reading the little information boards as you go rather than charging straight through. Plenty of them focus on British waters and the North Sea, which makes a nice link to the sea right outside the door. Pushchairs and grandparents generally find the compact layout easy to manage, and it's the kind of visit that doesn't wear everyone out before lunch.

Yarmouth has some brilliant extras to tie in with it. The Hippodrome Circus, built in 1903, is one of the very few purpose-built circus buildings still putting on shows in Britain, and its summer and Christmas seasons are a proper seaside tradition. For a rainy-day double bill, the Time and Tide Museum in the old town tells the story of the herring fishing industry that built the place, complete with a recreated Victorian street.

And of course, the Golden Mile has all the classic seaside trimmings, from the amusements and rock shops to chips eaten on the sea wall. Just be aware that some arcades along the front have adults-only 18+ areas, so keep the kids to the family sections.
